name: Baumkirchen
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful residential community in the Unterinntal with excellent connections to Schwaz and Innsbruck, offering stunning views of the Karwendelberge.
beschreibung:
Overview

Baumkirchen is a sun-blessed municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district, situated at an altitude of approximately 563 meters in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley. With around 1,250 residents, the village is nestled along the sunny Gnadenwald plateau on the northern bank of the Inn River, directly facing Volders. Located just five kilometers east of the historic salt town of Hall in Tirol and fifteen kilometers from Innsbruck, Baumkirchen charms visitors with its authentic rural character and sweeping vistas of the Inn Valley, Mount Glungezer, and the Tux Alps. Celebrated as the drinking water oasis of the Inn Valley, the village draws upon exceptionally pure alpine springs and combines historic landmarks with tranquil alpine landscapes.

History

Archaeological evidence of settlement in the area traces back to the Bronze and Hallstatt eras, spurred by artesian springs and fertile clay soils. The village was first documented around 1147 as Poumchirche, a name denoting a wooden church or a church nestled among trees. For centuries, Baumkirchen was spiritually linked with neighboring Mils. A prime historic monument is Schloss Wohlgemutsheim, built in 1474 by Paul Heuberger. In 1587, Archduke Ferdinand II of Tyrol acquired the castle for his consort Anna Caterina Gonzaga; later owned by the noble convent of Hall, it now operates as a retreat and educational center run by the Salesian Sisters of Don Bosco. During the 16th and 17th centuries, the Annabad mineral spa attracted noble patrons. Across from the historic bathhouse, the Early Baroque Saint Anne Chapel was built in 1645 based on designs by physician Dr. Hippolyt Guarinoni. The Gothic parish church of Saint Lawrence with its Late Baroque onion dome completes the historic village ensemble.

How to Get There

Motorists reach Baumkirchen via the Inntal motorway A12, exiting at Hall-Mitte or Volders/Wattens, and crossing the Inn River bridge via the B171 road within minutes. Rail travelers take the Tyrolean S-Bahn (lines S4 and S5) to Volders-Baumkirchen station, which operates half-hourly and is only fifteen minutes away from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof. Regional buses connect the village with Hall in Tirol and Wattens, while cyclists can use the Inn Cycle Path R1 running right along the river.

Tips

A delightful walk leads through the scenic Baumkirchen Valley along the babbling torrent past stone check dams up to the pristine drinking water springs. Culture enthusiasts can stroll from the village square past Saint Lawrence Church to the Saint Anne Chapel on Kreuzbühel and onwards to the grounds of Schloss Wohlgemutsheim. Longer hikes lead up to the sunny Gnadenwald plateau with its pilgrimage churches. In winter, the plateau offers cross-country skiing trails, while the Glungezer and Patscherkofel ski areas lie a short drive across the valley.
